newsitem.title: ITALY: Arafat to visit Italy on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to visit Italy on Tuesday.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will visit Italy on Tuesday on his first foreign trip since taking control of most of the West Bank town of Hebron in a landmark deal with Israel, PLO officials said on Monday.

Palestine Liberation Organisation representative Nemer Hammad said Arafat would address a meeting of the Socialist International in Rome and would later have talks with Prime Minister Romano Prodi and President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro.
Israel and the PLO signed the Hebron deal last week after months of negotiations and arm-twisting by the United States.

Arafat hailed the accord, in which Israeli troops withdrew from most of the town, as a liberation after 30 years of Israeli occupation and a "springboard...so that we can establish our independent Palestinian state".

Israel now controls one fifth of Hebron including the homes of 400 Jews, 20,000 Palestinians and the Tomb of the Patriarchs, a site holy to Jews and Moslems. It rejects the establishment of a Palestinian state, which it fears could endanger Israel.

Arafat had been due to travel to Florence for the inauguration of a photographic exhibition, "Bethlehem 2000", on Wednesday but Hammad said he would now no longer be attending because of the "delicate situation and the whole peace process".
"It is impossible," he said, adding Arafat would fly home from Italy on Tuesday evening.
